title: Equivalent Expressions by Graphing: Graph Match
description: Identify equivalent single-variable expressions by renaming the variable x when needed, graphing the original, and comparing each answer-choice graph, including expressions written in function notation.

questions.explanation_html: Rename t as x for graphing. On the stated domain, cancel the common factor \(t+3\). The remaining graph is \(2t-6\).
questions.variation: Graph a grouped fraction on its allowed domain

distractor_notes.A: Uses the sign of the canceled factor.

questions.explanation_html: Graph the whole radical using x in place of t. Factoring 4 inside the radical gives \(2\sqrt{t+6}\) on the allowed inputs.
questions.variation: Compare graphs with the whole radicand grouped

distractor_notes.A: Takes the full square factor outside the root.
distractor_notes.C: Takes one addend out of the radical.
distractor_notes.D: Scales only part of the radicand.

questions.stem_html: Which expression is equivalent to \(\left(\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}3]{x}\right)^{2}\) for every positive x?
questions.explanation_html: For positive x, the root has exponent \(1/3\). Raising to power 2 multiplies the exponents, giving \(x^{2/3}\). Their graphs agree on this domain.

distractor_notes.B: Reverses the numerator and denominator of the exponent.
distractor_notes.C: Multiplies the root index and power.
distractor_notes.D: Divides the root exponent by the outside power.

questions.stem_html: Let \(f(x)=2x+7\) and \(g(x)=x+3\). Which expression equals \(f(g(x))\) for all x?
questions.explanation_html: Enter the full nested expression or substitute the entire \(x+3\) for x in f. The result is \(2x+13\).
questions.variation: Graph a composition from supplied definitions

distractor_notes.D: Drops the outer scale on the variable.

questions.explanation_html: Group the full numerator and denominator before graphing. Factor f(x) as 3 times the product of \((x-4)\) and \((x+4)\). Cancel g(x) only on the stated domain.
questions.variation: Graph a quotient using both function definitions

distractor_notes.A: Keeps the wrong factor after cancellation.
distractor_notes.B: Drops the scale of the numerator.
distractor_notes.C: Graphs the numerator instead of the quotient.
